title: Burial before sunset
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the intensive care unit. It is Saturday. Mr Hussain, 74, died at 07:00 this morning from severe pneumonia. You looked after him during his admission. Before going off duty, the consultant confirmed that the cause of death is clear and that no referral to the coroner is needed.

At 08:30 his family ask whether his body can be released today, because their faith requires burial as soon as possible after death. The consultant has asked you to complete the medical certificate of cause of death.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Explain to the family what must happen before his body can be released, and that you'll try to do it quickly.
options.brief: Honest about the process, and shows the family you are taking their request seriously.
options.detailed: The family need to understand what is involved, including the certificate, its review by the medical examiner, and registration of the death, and they need to know you are trying to help. Many register offices offer urgent arrangements for burials that can't wait. Being clear about what you can and can't control prevents false promises while respecting the importance of their request.

options.text: Ask the bereavement office to help the family with the arrangements.
options.brief: The bereavement team knows the process and can coordinate with the family.
options.detailed: Bereavement officers are experienced in supporting families with urgent release and can liaise with the registrar and funeral directors. Involving them is helpful, though it ranks below the actions that only you can take.

options.text: Complete the death certificate promptly, and ask the medical examiner's office whether it can be prioritised.
options.brief: The practical steps that make same-day release possible.
options.detailed: The certificate must be reviewed by a medical examiner before registration. Many offices have arrangements for urgent release on religious grounds. Completing your part promptly and asking for priority gives the family the best chance of meeting their timescale.

options.text: Tell the family that same-day release isn't usually possible because of hospital procedures.
options.brief: May be inaccurate and closes the door before you have tried.
options.detailed: Procedures do take time, and same-day release isn't always achievable. But many hospitals can meet urgent requests, especially when no coroner referral is needed. Telling the family it isn't possible, before trying, may be wrong and adds to their distress.

options.text: Leave the death certificate until the consultant who knew him best is back on duty on Monday.
options.brief: Causes an avoidable delay of several days, when you are able to complete it.
options.detailed: You looked after Mr Hussain and can complete the certificate, as the consultant has asked. Leaving it until Monday would make the burial the family needs impossible, for no good reason.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you respond sensitively and practically to a family's religious needs after a death, working within the certification process.
explanation.keyDetails: The cause of death is clear and no coroner referral is needed. The family's faith requires burial as soon as possible. The consultant has asked you to complete the certificate.
explanation.reasoning: [A] explains honestly and commits to helping, [C] takes the practical steps that make release possible, and [B] brings in the bereavement team. [D] gives up too early, and [E] creates an avoidable delay.
explanation.competing: The ordering of [A] and [C] is close; you would do both within minutes. The key puts the conversation first because the family have asked directly and need to know what to expect.
